lead: a promise you made aloud, in front of witnesses, at an hour on a specific afternoon. every clause of it has held, including through the two years you were living somewhere else.
sun: leaving was never a decision about the promise. you went the way you go — no announcement, no date, the door on the latch — and came home glad, with no re-entry to perform, because by your own accounting nothing had been exited. the terms ran on unbroken while you were away. no one has had to forgive you for any of it, and it has not occurred to you to ask.
moon: the oath does not consult how anyone is feeling that year — that is its whole design, and it is why yours has held through absences it was never built for. release is the missing motion. nothing in you drafts the letter that ends an agreement, so the bond outlasts the arrangement it described and goes on being honoured after both of you stopped recognising it.
pull: you have never broken a promise and you have never finished one. the vow has held through two years of an empty house, and holding is the only thing it knows how to do.
tension: the marriage gets held up by other people as the one that worked, and it is accurate: three decades, no betrayal, every undertaking met. what none of them can see is which of you did the staying. she has spent whole years married to an obligation with nobody in the house, and no complaint is available to her — nothing was withheld, nothing was broken, and the thing she wanted was never written down.
cost: a promise given to you at twenty-five is still in force at fifty-five, in its original wording, unamended by anything that has happened since — so the undertakings nobody else will take on come to you. none of them has an end date. you are still serving two that the other party let you off years ago, and you did not hear yourself let off.

lead: every one of the nine who started this with you has had a last day. you have never had one, and that alone is why the room now waits to hear what you remember.
sun: your standing was not climbed to. you keep coming again — out for a year, out for three, and in again at the same place, so your run reads as unbroken to anybody who missed the gaps, and everybody who was there for them has gone. the others stopped on a stated day, and a stated day is what takes a name off the top of a list.
moon: seniority is a position, not an age, and it settled on you early without asking. the deference is for the date and not for the work. so every argument about what this was originally for comes to you, you draw the original up, and it is taken — nobody above you to check it against, so the version you produce becomes what happened.
pull: you can produce the original of anything here and be believed, because the date is yours. there is no one left holding an original of you.
tension: a vacancy is what the people behind you are waiting on, and your leaving does not produce one. you go, the room reorganises around whoever is left, and fourteen months later you are back at the same standing and it closes over. two of them have quit the field, warmly, saying generous things about you on the way out, and neither had anything to accuse you of — nothing was taken from them, you only kept declining to be finished.
cost: you are the reason the early period of this thing still exists — the material, the reasons behind it, people who would otherwise be a rumour, all of it retrievable from one person who never stopped being here. nothing comes the other direction. what you go down and get for everybody else, there is no one above you positioned to get for you.

lead: you found the town at twenty-six and the woman at twenty-nine, and neither of those was the bottom. what you were actually after was under both of them, and you are still going down.
sun: nothing about the beginning of you reads as historical. the year before you were born is a live year — reachable, still running, containing people who can be gone to — so you did not research it, you went and resumed it. letters got answered, visits happened, and after each silence you started again, because a stretch of no contact only ever means somebody has not surfaced yet.
moon: underneath, an answer is only ever a floor, and floors here come up when you push. she gave you the reason, the reason had a reason, and that one had a household behind it and a decision made in a bad decade by people who are findable. you cannot look at a cause without lifting what grew out of it, and nothing in you rules that this is deep enough.
pull: every answer you have been given was a lid. you keep lifting them, and what is under there has not aged — it is down there working, and it comes up with you.
tension: she had it arranged: a matter closed in her twenties, a husband who knows a shortened version, adult children who know none of it. then someone who cannot let a thing be finished, coming again every eighteen months with something else found. she has never once refused you, and that is the difficulty. what you are owed and what she can survive being asked have never been the same size. her life was built assuming you stayed down there.
cost: give you a thing three people have already explained plausibly and you will come up with the actual cause, and be right, and the ones who needed it right will say so for years. the plant does not go into the ground again. what surfaces with you arrives current — settled decades ago, still able to do the work it did then.

lead: the hall meets on thursdays and has for twenty-two years. you have been leaving it and coming into it that entire time, often in the same season, and never once been simply inside it.
sun: your comings and goings do not resolve into a membership anybody can dispute, because you always turn up again and the turning up is what gets recorded. the woman who stopped attending over the same objection you made twice is spoken of as having left. you made it, went, and were at the table within a season, so nothing you did got written down as a departure at all.
moon: the room reads as one animal from outside and it is not one — half arriving, half on its way out, and you are the only person there who has been counted in both halves. so you know where the doorway is from either side, and can put a lapsed person back among people in one evening. standing in a doorway is not being in the room.
pull: the hall has never had all of you in it. your being at the next thursday is the one certainty in that room, and half of you will be walking toward the door.
tension: the ones who went and were let stay gone have a case they cannot make, since the rule was never written and has only been applied to them. what the room says about you is that you always come home to it — warm, accurate, and a description of something you do not control. your objection pays for it. you make the same one every few years, and it arrives as the noise a person makes on the way out.
cost: you can bring somebody who has been out for years into a room full of people and have them received inside an hour, because you know the walk in both directions and have never made anyone account for either. the same competence is why no thursday of yours has been spent all the way in. the door is a permanent part of where you stand.
